question.prompt: There are a total of numCourses courses you have to take, labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1. You are given an array prerequisites where prerequisites[i] = [a_i, b_i] indicates that you must take b_i first if you want to take a_i. Return true if you can finish all courses, otherwise return false.
expectedPoints: Model problem as Cycle Detection in a Directed Graph
Propose either Kahn's algorithm (BFS with in-degrees) or DFS with 3-state coloring (unvisited, visiting, visited)
Build adjacency list and compute in-degrees for each vertex
Analyze O(V + E) time and O(V + E) space complexity
Discuss disconnected components, self-loops, and empty prerequisites
commonMistakes: Confusing undirected cycle detection (union-find) with directed graphs

transcript: Candidate: This problem maps directly to detecting a cycle in a directed graph, or determining if a valid topological ordering exists. If there is a directed cycle, it is impossible to finish all courses. I recommend Kahn's algorithm using BFS and an in-degree array. First, we initialize an adjacency list of size V and an inDegree array of size V initialized to 0. For every pair [course, prereq], we add course to adj[prereq] and increment inDegree[course]. Next, we push all nodes with inDegree 0 into a BFS queue. While the queue has elements, we pop a course, increment our visitedCount, and for each neighbor in adj[course], we decrement its inDegree. If inDegree drops to 0, we enqueue it. Finally, if visitedCount equals numCourses, return true; otherwise a cycle prevented all courses from resolving, so return false. Time complexity is O(V + E) because we process each vertex and edge once. Space complexity is O(V + E) for the adjacency list and queue. Edge cases: self-dependency [0, 0], disconnected DAG components, and empty prerequisites array.
notes: Flawless execution of Kahn algorithm. Edge direction, in-degree logic, O(V+E) complexities, and edge cases all explicitly addressed.
